introduction.purpose: This Technical Design Document defines the system architecture, data models, API contracts, and deployment strategy for the Online Learning Management System (LMS). It serves as the authoritative reference for development teams implementing the platform.
introduction.scope: Covers the full backend and frontend architecture for user management, course lifecycle, enrollment, content delivery, assessment, messaging, payments, and analytics.
assumptions: All video content is hosted on AWS S3 with CloudFront CDN distribution
Stripe handles all payment processing with webhook-based enrollment triggers
PostgreSQL is the primary relational database
Redis is used for session management and caching
Deployment target is AWS (ECS + RDS + S3)
constraints: Node.js backend with Python AI/analytics microservice

tech_stack.frontend: React.js 18, MUI v5, Redux Toolkit, Axios
tech_stack.infrastructure: AWS ECS (Fargate), RDS, S3, CloudFront, SES, SQS

system_architecture.overview: The LMS follows a layered microservices architecture with a React SPA frontend, a Node.js API gateway, domain-specific microservices, and managed AWS infrastructure. Services communicate via REST APIs internally and use SQS for async jobs like email dispatch.
system_architecture.communication: REST over HTTPS for synchronous calls; AWS SQS for asynchronous jobs (email, certificate generation)

data_model.overview: Relational schema using PostgreSQL. All tables use UUID primary keys. Soft deletes via deleted_at timestamp. Optimistic locking for concurrent updates on enrollments and grades.

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stores all user accounts (students, instructors, admins)

tables.name: courses
tables.purpose: Course catalog with metadata and publishing state

tables.name: enrollments
tables.purpose: Tracks which students are enrolled in which courses

tables.name: lessons
tables.purpose: Individual lessons within a module (video, text, quiz)

columns.name: video_url
columns.description: S3 presigned URL or CloudFront URL

tables.name: certificates
tables.purpose: Certificates issued to students who pass a course

columns.name: certificate_url
columns.description: S3 URL of generated PDF certificate

api_design.overview: RESTful API using JSON. All authenticated endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <JWT> header. Versioned under /api/v1.
api_design.authentication: JWT Bearer tokens (Access: 15min, Refresh: 7 days) via Authorization header

component_architecture.overview: Frontend is a React SPA with Redux Toolkit for global state. Backend services are domain-isolated Node.js modules sharing a common PostgreSQL connection pool.

non_functional_requirements.performance: API P95 response time < 500ms. Video delivery via CloudFront CDN for < 2s time-to-first-byte globally. Horizontal scaling via ECS Fargate. Redis caching for course listings and user profiles.
non_functional_requirements.scalability: Stateless microservices deployable on ECS Fargate with auto-scaling policies. PostgreSQL read replicas for analytics queries. SQS-based async processing for email and certificate generation prevents blocking.
non_functional_requirements.security: JWT RS256 signed tokens. bcrypt (cost 12) for password hashing. All data encrypted at rest (AES-256 RDS) and in transit (TLS 1.3). GDPR: right to erasure via soft delete + scheduled data purge. FERPA: audit logs for all grade access.
non_functional_requirements.availability: 99.9% SLA achieved via multi-AZ RDS, ECS multi-AZ task placement, and Route53 health checks with failover. Graceful degradation: video delivery independent of API availability via CloudFront.
non_functional_requirements.maintainability: Modular microservice architecture. Each service has isolated DB schema access. OpenAPI 3.0 auto-generated docs. Structured logging with correlation IDs. Centralized error handling middleware.
non_functional_requirements.compliance: GDPR: data minimization, consent management, right to erasure, data export. FERPA: access controls on grade data, audit trail. PCI-DSS: no card data stored (Stripe handles all card data).

deployment_architecture.overview: AWS-based containerized deployment using ECS Fargate for all services, RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ for the database, ElastiCache Redis, and S3 + CloudFront for media.
deployment_architecture.infrastructure: AWS ECS Fargate (microservices), RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ, ElastiCache Redis cluster, S3 (media + backups), CloudFront (CDN), SQS (async jobs), SES → SendGrid (email), Route53 + ACM (DNS + TLS)
deployment_architecture.ci_cd: GitHub Actions: lint → unit tests → integration tests → Docker build → ECR push → ECS rolling deploy. Blue/green deployment strategy via CodeDeploy. Environment promotion: dev → staging → production.
deployment_architecture.monitoring: CloudWatch for infrastructure metrics and logs. Datadog APM for distributed tracing across services. PagerDuty alerts for P1 incidents. Sentry for frontend error tracking.

traceability_matrix.fdd_requirement: FR-001: The system shall allow users to register an account with email and password.
FR-002: The system shall allow users to log in using email/password or OAuth.
FR-007: Instructors shall be able to create a new course.
FR-014: Students shall be able to search and browse available courses.
FR-016: Students must complete payment via Stripe before enrolling in paid courses.
FR-020: The system must track lesson completion for each student.
FR-024: The system shall allow students to submit assignments as file uploads.
FR-027: Students shall receive a certificate upon finishing with >= 60% grade.
FR-032: Admin shall view platform-level analytics.
